THESE APPEALS, COMING ON FOR FINAL HEARING, THIS DAY, THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 JUDGMENT 1.

The claimants as well as the insurer are in appeal challenging the compensation of Rs.13,35,000/-
awarded for the death of Basha Sab.

2. It is the contention of the insurer that the police were informed that Basha Sab was vomiting blood profusely, since his Blood Pressure had increased and on the basis of this information the police prepared an unnatural death report which was produced as Annexure- R1.
3.
It is also stated that the Medical Register also indicated that Basha Sab was brought dead to the hospital.
It is highlighted that Kaleel, co-brother of deceased, who was brought on record did not choose to lodge any complaint about the motor vehicle accident as indicated in the claim petition.
4. It is also stated that according to the claimants the deceased was hit by a mini bus and the driver of the mini bus abandoned the vehicle and ran away from the spot.
But the evidence on record does not indicate that any vehicle was found at the spot and therefore, this was a clear case of fraudulent claim put forth.
5. The deceased was subjected to Post Mortem and the Post Mortem report has been produced as Ex.P-4.
This Post Mortem report indicates that the death was due to chest injuries sustained.

However, no opinion is recorded as to whether this could have been caused due to a motor vehicle accident.
6.

In my view, having regard to the contention advanced by the insurer, it would be appropriate to remand the matter to the Tribunal reserving liberty to the insurer to summon the Doctors, who conducted the Post Mortem to elicit the cause of death.
The insurer would also be entitled to adduce such other evidence as is available to establish that the death did not occur due to a motor vehicle accident.
7. Liberty is also reserved to the claimants to adduce evidence to establish that the accident occurred as a result of the motor vehicle accident.
The appeals are allowed accordingly.
8. The impugned award is set aside and the matter is remitted to the Tribunal forthwith for fresh consideration.
9. Since the parties are represented by the counsel, they shall appear before the Tribunal on 24.05.2023 and take further instructions.
10. The Tribunal shall endeavour to consider the matter within a period of six months.
